# `Q-20-7` — Theorem Has No Registered Theorem Type For Its Identifier

> A theorem-family block's identifier prefix is a recognized
> cross-reference type, but not one registered as a theorem type.

## What this means

A theorem, lemma, corollary, or similar block's identifier (e.g.
`#fig-x`) starts with a prefix Quarto recognizes as a cross-reference
type in general, but that prefix does not belong to the theorem-type
family the block's class implies. Quarto 1 would abort the whole render
in this situation; the pandoc-leg shim instead renders the block as a
plain, unstyled div without theorem numbering, so the document still
builds. Any `@ref` to that block will not resolve to a number, since
none was assigned.

## Why this happens

- A theorem-family div's identifier accidentally used another
  cross-reference family's prefix (for example a figure prefix like
  `fig-`) instead of a theorem prefix.
- The block's class (`.theorem`, `.lemma`, `.corollary`, and similar)
  does not match the cross-reference family its identifier's prefix
  actually belongs to.

## How to fix

Give the block an identifier prefix registered as a theorem type (for
example `thm-`, `lem-`, `cor-`, `def-`, `exm-`, `exr-`), matching the
theorem-family class you used, or change the class to match whichever
cross-reference family the identifier's prefix actually belongs to.

## Related errors

- [`Q-20-6`](Q-20-6.qmd) — the same shape of fallback for a callout
  whose identifier prefix is not a registered numbering category,
  rather than a theorem block whose identifier does not match a
  theorem type.
